analysis:
Examined both configuration excerpts, registry metadata, patch and BASE source against the canonical definition index and supplied T-041 detail. No concrete security regression is established by this documentation-only evidence. Configuration.md:568 changes reclaimable-memory accounting while preserving separate reserves and a fail-closed free-only policy; :579–603 describes uncached hashing, page-cache dropping and replacement of GLM bracketing verification with loader-produced per-file SHA-256. Model-registry-format.md HEAD:119–122 adds page-cache dropping without changing aggregate digest ordering, manifest authority, publication authorization or billing. Surrounding cache, media, runtime and attestation controls do not change in the supplied range map; their historical risks are not new findings.
Material integration questions remain under A-004, TB-003, TB-007, T-012 and T-027: configuration.md:371 (visible orientation patch) introduces persistent verified-weight records reused during startup registration. Review VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift and its callers to establish how records remain trustworthy against the adversarial operator; owner-only permissions and filesystem fingerprints alone do not establish that contract. Also examine WeightHasher.swift, PageCache.swift and managed GLM load/publication paths to verify that the published aggregate covers the actual loaded bytes, that failures prevent identity publication, and that replacing pre/post-load passes does not weaken mutation detection. Review SystemMemory.swift admission interactions for bounded arithmetic, failed sampling and exclusion of anonymous/compressed memory. These implementations are outside this batch, so neither their safety nor a missing control is inferred. T-041's salt isolation, HMAC names, TTL and encrypted-storage mitigations show no supplied change.
